mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to the prior month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Federal Reserve cut rates in September and October 2007
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines relative to the prior month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and residential construction (HOUST) relative to the prior month signals a broad-based economic contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where both INDPRO and HOUST decline from the prior month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.8% signals an economic slowdown that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and UNRATE > 4.8%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where CPIAUCSL (YoY) > 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening cycle (UNRATE < 4.5%), a monthly decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 100,000 additions signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate hiring and revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS (monthly change) < 100,000, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential construction (HOUST) relative to the prior month signals weak housing demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where HOUST declines from the prior month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 1.0% signals weak consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where RSAFS (monthly change) < -1.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
